h1: How Much Does a Photo Booth Rental Cost in NYC?
excerpt: There's no single sticker price for a photo booth in NYC — here's what actually moves the number, so you know what you're paying for before you ask for a quote.

heroImg.alt: Photo booth set up at an event in New York City

body.heading: Why there's no flat rate
paragraphs: Ask five photo booth companies what a rental costs and you'll get five different answers, and honestly, ours would be five different answers too depending on your event. That's not evasiveness — it's because a photo booth quote is built from several moving parts, not read off a single price list. The booth type you pick, how many hours you need it running, how far it has to travel, and which add-ons you want all move the number independently.

That said, you shouldn't have to fill out a form just to get a sense of scale. Our Studio Booth, one of our most-booked options, starts at $899 for 3 hours. That's a real starting point, not a teaser rate — custom packages (longer rentals, premium booths, branded activations) are priced to the event itself, which is why we don't post a single ceiling number. What follows is what actually moves the price up or down from that starting point, so a quote makes sense the moment it lands in your inbox.

body.heading: Booth type is the biggest factor
paragraphs: The booth itself is usually the largest single driver of price. A full-length mirror booth with an animated touchscreen and studio lighting is a different piece of equipment — and a different install — than a roaming photo booth, where an attendant simply walks the room with a handheld capture system and there's no structure to set up at all. A branded booth built around a custom wrap, start screen and campaign overlays carries more production than a standard rental, and something like a mosaic wall, where every guest photo prints as a sticker that builds into one giant image, is its own category of setup and output entirely.

None of these are "better" or "worse" — they're suited to different rooms and different goals. That's why the fastest way to a realistic number is telling us what the event actually is; we'll recommend a booth to fit it rather than starting from a price and working backward.

body.heading: Hours, and what happens outside them
paragraphs: How long you book the booth for is the second-biggest lever, and most events don't need it running all night — three to four hours is typical for a wedding reception, and it's usually better spent live during the highest-energy stretch than sitting idle earlier in the evening. If your event runs long and you want the booth to keep going, additional hours beyond what you booked are $125 per hour.

One thing worth knowing up front: our team arrives about an hour before your scheduled start time to set up and test everything. If you need us on site earlier than that — for early venue access or extra setup time — an idle fee of $150 per hour applies. It's not a penalty, it's just the honest cost of an attendant standing by rather than driving to another booking.

body.heading: Travel and your borough
paragraphs: We're based in Brooklyn and serve Brooklyn, Manhattan, Queens, the Bronx, Staten Island, Long Island, Westchester, New Jersey and Connecticut. Travel is quoted from your venue's ZIP code before you book, so it's part of your upfront number rather than a surprise on the invoice — a Williamsburg wedding and a Westchester one simply won't carry the same travel line, and we'll tell you which up front.

body.heading: Add-ons that change the number
paragraphs: Custom print templates built around your names, date or logo are standard on most bookings. Beyond that, things like a flower wall or champagne wall as a backdrop, branded overlays and a microsite for a corporate activation, or an extra roaming attendant to cover seated tables at a large wedding all add to the quote — and all are optional, so you're never paying for something you didn't ask for.

Every rental, regardless of booth or add-ons, includes a trained on-site attendant, unlimited prints for your guests, and our $3 million liability policy with a same-day certificate of insurance if your venue needs one. Those aren't upsells — they're built into every quote we send.

Because pricing is genuinely specific to your date, venue and booth choice, the fastest way to a real number is our quote form — it takes about 30 seconds and comes back with pricing built for your actual event, travel included.

A trained on-site attendant, unlimited prints for your guests during your rental, and our $3 million liability policy with a same-day certificate of insurance if your venue requires one. Travel is calculated from your venue's ZIP code and included in the quote up front, not added later.

h1: Corporate Event Photo Booth Ideas That Actually Get Used
excerpt: The difference between a corporate photo booth people actually line up for and one that sits empty in the corner usually comes down to a handful of decisions made before the event.

heroImg.alt: Branded photo booth activation at a corporate event in New York

body.heading: Start with what the event needs to do
paragraphs: A photo booth does a different job depending on who the event is for. At an internal event — a holiday party, a summer outing, an awards night — it gives coworkers who don't otherwise talk a reason to stand together, and everyone leaves with something to take home. At an external event — a product launch, a trade show stand, a brand activation — the booth becomes a marketing channel. Every photo that leaves carries your branding out to an audience the attendee already trusts, which is distribution you can't buy directly.
Deciding which of those two jobs your event needs first changes almost every choice that follows, from which booth to book to how much lead time to plan for.

body.heading: Branding the whole experience, not just the backdrop
paragraphs: A branded photo booth can be wrapped entirely in your colors, with a custom start screen, branded photo overlays, custom-printed backdrops, and a hosted online gallery or microsite for the images. The reason this matters more at a corporate event than a private one: a generic booth sitting in the middle of a carefully branded activation undermines the rest of the spend. Consistency is the actual product.

Lead time matters here. A full physical wrap needs two to three weeks' notice so graphics can be printed and applied correctly. If your date is closer than that, digital-only branding — the start screen, overlays and gallery — turns around considerably faster and still carries the brand through every photo.

body.heading: Make it collect something, not just photos
paragraphs: Surveys and short questionnaires can be built directly into the booth flow, so you're gathering product feedback at the exact moment attendees are engaged rather than emailing them a week later when the event has left their mind. Opt-in contact capture builds a compliant list for remarketing, and you receive a report of what was collected — the images and any data captured belong to you, not us.

That turns the booth into an activation you can put numbers against afterward: engagement volume, opt-in rate, shares. That's a very different conversation with a marketing lead than "people seemed to like it."

body.heading: Picking the right booth for the room
paragraphs: For a multi-day trade show or a conference floor where footfall is spread across a full day rather than concentrated into one evening, a roaming photo booth usually outperforms a static one — an attendant works the aisle with a handheld capture system instead of waiting for a line to form at a fixed booth. For an internal celebration where you want one big collective moment, a mosaic wall is worth considering: every guest's photo prints as a sticker they place themselves, and by the end of the night the wall has built into one large image, often a company logo. For a launch or sponsored activation where the branding has to be airtight, the branded booth — full wrap, custom start screen, overlays and microsite — is built for exactly that.

body.heading: Handling the venue logistics
paragraphs: Midtown offices, hotel ballrooms, convention centers and gallery spaces all come with their own loading dock windows, freight elevator bookings, building engineers and certificate-of-insurance requirements. We handle that coordination as a matter of course, planning load-in around your venue's actual access rather than the floor plan on paper — and we carry a $3 million policy, so the COI paperwork is rarely the thing holding up approval.

faqs.q: Can you invoice our company and work to a PO?
faqs.a: Yes, we work with corporate clients regularly. For established accounts we can also arrange payment terms — an opening order of $5,000 or more is required to set an account up.

faqs.q: How much notice do you need for a fully branded booth?
faqs.a: Two to three weeks for a physical wrap, since graphics have to be printed and applied. Digital branding — the start screen, overlays and gallery — can be produced much faster if your date is closer than that.

faqs.q: Do we own the photos and any data collected?
faqs.a: Yes. Images and any opt-in contact data gathered at your activation belong to you. We provide the gallery and the report, and you decide what happens with it next.

faqs.q: Which booth works best for a trade show?
faqs.a: For a multi-day show with footfall spread across the day, the roaming photo booth usually covers more ground than a static booth, since an attendant brings the camera to people rather than waiting for a line.
Yes. A trained attendant runs every booth for the full length of your rental — setup, guest assistance and breakdown — so nobody from your own team has to manage it.

meta.title: How to Choose a Wedding Photo Booth | Magic Mirror Brooklyn
meta.description: Which photo booth suits a wedding, when to run it during your reception, and what your NYC venue will need — a practical guide for couples planning theirs.

h1: How to Choose a Wedding Photo Booth in NYC
excerpt: The right wedding photo booth depends less on which one looks nicest online and more on your guest list, your venue, and when you run it — here's how to think it through.

heroImg.alt: Bride and groom posing at the wedding photo booth in New York City

body.heading: Why a photo booth earns its place at a wedding
paragraphs: Your photographer captures the day. A photo booth captures what your guests did with it — the table of cousins who piled in six at a time, the uncle who found the boa, the friends who came back four times over the night. Those are different photographs, and you generally only get them if there's a booth in the room.

There's a practical argument too. A booth keeps the room busy during the flat spots — the gap between dinner and dancing, the stretch while the band changes over — and gives guests who aren't dancing somewhere to be. Couples routinely tell us their guests stayed later than expected, and the booth is usually part of why.

body.heading: When to run it during your reception
paragraphs: Most weddings book three to four hours of booth time. The sweet spot is opening as cocktail hour ends and running through the heart of the dance floor, so the booth is live while the energy is highest rather than sitting idle through dinner speeches.

If your reception runs long, it's usually better to start the booth later than to start it early and have it close before the night peaks. Talk this through with your booth company when you get a quote, rather than just defaulting to more hours than you need.

body.heading: Matching the booth to your wedding
paragraphs: The mirror booth is the most-booked choice for weddings, largely because the full-length format handles whole wedding parties at once and works for every generation in the room, from the flower girl to the grandparents. The glam booth suits black-tie weddings where you want the photos to look as considered as the outfits — a black-and-white, skin-smoothing look closer to a red-carpet shot than a snapshot. The 360 booth, where a slow-motion camera orbits your guests on a lit platform, has become the pick for younger, more shareable crowds.

For guest lists over about 150, it's worth pairing a static booth with a roaming attendant so the seated tables get covered too, rather than everyone funneling into one queue at the same booth all night.

body.heading: What your venue will need from you
paragraphs: Most NYC wedding venues ask for a certificate of insurance naming them as additionally insured before they'll confirm your vendor. A $3 million policy with same-day COI turnaround is worth confirming with any booth company you're considering — it's one less thing to chase in the weeks before the wedding.

On the setup side, plan for the booth to arrive about an hour before your start time and take roughly 20 minutes to set up. A 10ft x 10ft footprint is ideal, 8ft x 8ft is the minimum, and it needs a standard outlet within 15 feet that isn't already shared with the DJ or catering. Flagging this with your venue coordinator early avoids a last-minute scramble for power.

faqs.q: How many hours should we book for a wedding?
faqs.a: Three to four hours covers most receptions. Rather than sell you an extra hour you don't need, we'd rather help you place those hours well — tell us your run sheet and we'll suggest a start time.

faqs.q: Can the booth match our wedding colors?
faqs.a: Yes. The print template is designed around your names, date and palette, and you choose the backdrop from our range. A flower wall is also available if you want the backdrop to be part of the decor rather than just behind it.

faqs.q: Which booth do most couples book?
faqs.a: The mirror booth is our most-booked wedding option because its full-length format works for entire wedding parties and every age in the room. The glam booth suits black-tie weddings, and the 360 booth tends to draw younger, more shareable crowds.

faqs.q: Do we get all the photos afterward?
faqs.a: Yes. Every image from the night lands in an online gallery you can download in full and share with guests, on top of the unlimited prints handed out at the reception.

faqs.q: How much space and power does the booth need?
faqs.a: A 10ft x 10ft space is ideal, 8ft x 8ft is the minimum, plus a standard outlet within 15 feet that isn't shared with the DJ or catering. We'll confirm this against your specific venue before the day.

faqs.q: Are you insured for our venue's requirements?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million liability policy, and if your venue needs a certificate of insurance naming them as additionally insured, we turn it around the same day you send their contact details.
